title: Planning reads a goal clause that names a constant against what the constant bounds
goal: The /kb-sprint plan step's clause-to-check mapping asks, for a goal clause that names a code constant (such as LAUNCH_BUDGET_S), what the constant bounds in the code, and rewrites a clause that asks it to bound something else before the start gate; found by the SP-kjqdiudr close: ST-bgfsi3n2 asked for a run file within LAUNCH_BUDGET_S (0.5 s), which bounds the launcher's return, and closed with the clause unmet as written. Also: a goal's time or share figure names the run it was measured on (profiled or not, which host, warm or cold) and the premise measures that run (SP-yzgetyu2: ST-s6tqojsw's 'about a third of today's 6.3 s' took a cProfile baseline while the work was timed unprofiled, 3.97 s to 2.2 s); and each run figure a goal names (row counts, subsets, arms, reps, effort levels) maps to a flag of the command that runs it, or the clause is rewritten or a flag task added before the start gate (SP-hm4qgf3t: ST-ji32ouga's 20-row web subset and opus-5-5 sanity subset that benchmarks.py run pool could not select, found as its gate g2 mid-work).

run:
import sys
r = lambda p: open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
sp, doc = r('.claude/skills/kb-sprint/SKILL.md'), r('kb/_self/backlog.md')
got = {'plan step reads constants in goal clauses': 'names a constant' in sp,
       'plan step and Sprints say a figure names the run': 'names the run' in sp and 'names the run' in doc,
       'plan step and Sprints map a run figure to a flag': all('a flag of the command that runs it' in t for t in (sp, doc))}
print(got)
sys.exit(0 if all(got.values()) else 1)

notes: Merged at the 2026-10-10 backlog triage (full text in git history): ST-dufjnho5 (a goal figure names its run) and ST-fumnrmll (a run figure maps to a flag); their scope is in the goal. Planned at the 2026-10-10 whole-backlog triage, which the operator asked to end with every draft planned into a sprint or dropped (sprint 11 of 13, "Planning rules 1: checks that run behaviour, touches that hold every reader"); it blocks no fitness test and no real user reported it, so it sits in a late sprint of the sequence. Premise: the plan step and backlog.md Sprints lack the three wordings the goal adds; the item's check reads them and fails now. Docs-only item, so its check reads doc text by nature. Premise run on the base 2026-10-10: all three wording tests False, exit 1.
